records.label: Signals from Singapore · updated 24 November 2026
records.title: Mapping AI governance frameworks across borders.
records.summary: At the 3rd Singapore-China Digital Policy Dialogue in Singapore on 22 November 2026, co-chaired by Senior Minister of State Tan Kiat How and National Data Administration Administrator Liu Liehong, MDDI said IMDA and the China Academy of Information and Communications Technology (CAICT) had completed a joint mapping of Singapore's AI Verify Testing Framework against CAICT's AI - Safety and Governance - Capability Requirements for System Risk Management Standard. The mapping, announced during Prime Minister Lawrence Wong's meeting with Premier Li Qiang on 21 November, is meant to help businesses navigate both frameworks by identifying corresponding safeguards and avoiding duplicative efforts. MDDI also said IMDA and the Cyberspace Administration of China held a technical meeting on AI governance and safety on 18 November and agreed to explore further cooperation. The mapping is a framework cross-reference, not mutual recognition or a single standard; further cooperation is stated as exploratory.

records.label: Signals from Singapore · updated 19 November 2026
records.title: Making trust interoperable for AI agents.
records.summary: On 17 November 2026, at the unveiling of the StableX Agentic Network, Senior Minister of State Tan Kiat How said AI agents need a verifiable identity, a clear mandate and continuous assurance, and that trust must work across systems and borders through open, interoperable approaches. He pointed to MetaComp's Know Your Agent (KYA) framework under the industry-led StableX network, MAS's work with financial institutions and AI firms on Safeguards for Agentic Finance at Runtime (SAFR), GovTech's Whole-of-Government Agentic Risk & Capability Framework and its GovHarness infrastructure, which is in development, and IMDA's work with industry partners to explore whether existing internet infrastructure such as the Domain Name System could support agent identification. He invited industry to collaborate on interoperable KYA arrangements, continuous assurance and trusted transactions in real-world environments. These are stated approaches, early-stage work and invitations; outcomes remain to be tracked.

records.label: Signals from Singapore · updated 16 November 2026
records.title: From individual AI use to enterprise adoption, with assurance.
records.summary: In opening remarks in Washington DC on 13 November 2026, Minister Josephine Teo said individual AI usage in Singapore is among the highest in the world on a per capita basis, and that for companies like OpenAI, “the next opportunity is to translate this strong individual adoption into enterprise use.” She said OpenAI is building up a sizeable team of forward-deployed engineers in Singapore, and that Anthropic decided it would grow a significant presence in Singapore and is very interested in working with Singapore on strengthening AI assurance. She also said Singapore, which becomes ASEAN Chair in 2027, is setting up a programme called ASEAN AI for All, with themes of AI adoption, AI assurance, innovative uses of AI and data foundations. In a 4 November 2026 written parliamentary answer, MDDI said IMDA is studying, in a workgroup with SWDA and industry partners, how AI adoption is reshaping tech jobs, hiring trends and skills requirements, and that IMDA will assess Bridge2Tech through students' participation and employment outcomes. These are stated plans, studies and company intentions; outcomes remain to be tracked.

records.label: Signals from Singapore · updated 14 November 2026
records.title: From pilots to enterprise-wide AI, with guardrails.
records.summary: Recent public signals pair wider AI adoption with testing and safeguards. On 27 October 2026 the Government announced a first cohort of 24 companies under the Champions of AI initiative, which supports enterprise-wide AI transformation. In 4 November 2026 parliamentary replies, MDDI said IMDA and CSA are studying how to strengthen the reporting of serious AI-related incidents, and pointed to the AI Verify Foundation's AI Tester Accreditation Programme and Singapore's proposal for ISO/IEC 42119-8 on testing methodologies for Generative AI systems. At the GovTech STACK Conference on 5 November, Senior Minister of State Tan Kiat How said GovTech's Agentic Risk and Capability (ARC) Framework connects an agent's capabilities to appropriate safeguards, with stronger controls such as human approval for higher-risk actions; that GovTech is developing GovHarness as shared infrastructure for building and operating AI agents across Government; and that Rabbit Deploy supports over 8,000 users across 90 agencies. These are studies, stated plans and platform descriptions; outcomes remain to be tracked.

records.label: Signals from Singapore · updated 6 October 2026
records.title: From AI capacity to real-world value.
records.summary: Recent public signals put a practical test at the centre of Singapore’s AI agenda: can organisations turn capacity into redesigned workflows and demonstrable value? A 5 October speech also described an ecosystem built around trust, talent and solutions developed, deployed and adapted in Singapore. These are stated priorities; evidence of outcomes is still the next thing to track.
